steps.title: A pop-up to change
steps.body: Every enemy runs on a brain, and every brain is a class: Pebblespout's is PopUp, which extends EnemyBrain, which extends Brain. Here you make your own: a pop-up that spits three fireballs each time it comes up. First, place a Pebblespout from the Starter pack, ahead of the start.

steps.title: Read about PopUp
steps.body: In Logic, under Built-in › Brains, press PopUp. It says what it extends (PopUp extends EnemyBrain extends Brain), its own hooks (spits, shotKind) and the ones it inherits (canSee, canAttack, attackPower, shouldFlee from EnemyBrain; nextState from Brain).

steps.title: Three fireballs
steps.body: Press Extend and write it: a Shots field, spits returns it, shotKind returns "fireball", and On state change (stateChange) says so in the Console as it rises. Every other decision stays PopUp's.

code: shots = field.number(3, { label: "Shots each time up", min: 1, max: 10 });

steps.title: Give Pebblespout the new brain
steps.body: In Characters, Pebblespout's Behaviour tab: + Script → My PopUp. Its PopUp row (built-in, extends EnemyBrain › Brain) holds EnemyBrain's settings: sight, power, the tell, and its kind of fighter.

steps.title: Practice fire
steps.body: Three fireballs a time is a lot. In the PopUp row, set Power to 0.5 (half a heart a fireball) while you practise: it is EnemyBrain's field, the same setting as Stats › Fights the hero, and it reaches Pebblespout through its line.

steps.title: Watch it spit
steps.body: Press Play and stand back. Pebblespout comes up (the Console says so), spits three fireballs and ducks. Step aside, raise your shield or bounce one back, and hit it while it is up.
steps.task: Press Play and wait for it to come up.

steps.title: Done!
steps.body: Every enemy works this way. Knight.shouldCounter, Turret.trackSpeed (a gaze you can outrun), Charger.shouldCharge, Flyer.circleTime, Ambusher.shouldDrop, Ghost.hiddenFor, PackHunter.callsPack, and from EnemyBrain canSee, canAttack, attackPower and shouldFlee for all of them. nextState can send any brain to another state.
